note: The fuzz harness enables PROXY protocol parsing unconditionally, so v1 and v2 prefixes are both reachable from raw input.
The input must also contain a complete HTTP request terminator to reach the HTTP parser after the proxy header.
The request bytes are first dispatched to the proxy parser before any HTTP method or path processing.

code: end = memchr(buffer, '\r', line_size); if (!end || end[1] != '\n') return NULL;
note: The v1 parser searches only a bounded line and rejects malformed delimiters, so the exploit needs a syntactically valid but boundary-stressing line.
The parser destructively splits the attacker-controlled line in place, so unusually long or malformed fields affect later field extraction.

code: inet_pton(...) and parse_ascii_port(...) populate request->proxy from the parsed fields
note: If the fields are parsed successfully, the source and destination addresses are written into the request context and the parser advances past the proxy header.
HTTP parsing resumes immediately after the proxy header, so a crafted header length or malformed line can shift the HTTP parser onto attacker-chosen bytes.
